A brokered GIC in your name can share a coverage limit with your direct deposits

Four charts group hypothetical eligible deposits by issuing CDIC member and category, combining direct and client-name brokered balances before applying a limit.

By TickerLantern Research · Published 25 October 2026 · 6 min read
Sources reviewed 25 October 2026

Change an assumption. Follow the result.

Group eligible balances by issuing member and coverage category

Interactive planning lab

Entered eligible deposit balances$340,000
Within the four assumed coverage-bucket limits$320,000
Above the individual bucket limits$20,000

Original same-date snapshot, using CDIC public guidance reviewed 25 October 2026 and a CAD 100,000 principal-plus-interest limit for each included qualifying category at each member. A and B are hypothetical and assumed to be genuinely distinct CDIC member institutions. One depositor owns all modeled balances. Only the one-name non-registered category and the separate TFSA eligible-deposit category are included. Every input is independently assumed to be an eligible deposit, includes interest accrued to the common observation date, and is held in client name. Direct and client-name brokered deposits in the same member/category are combined before applying the cap. Nominee-name deposits, trusts, joint accounts, other registered categories, foreign-currency conversion and provincial insurance schemes require their own rules and are excluded. A statement, platform, broker, branch, product name or account count does not establish a separate issuing member. No actual product eligibility or ownership record is verified. This is not a contribution-room calculation, transfer instruction, payout forecast, credit-risk estimate or maturity/access calendar. Future interest and balance movements are not projected. An amount above a modeled cap is not a predicted loss.

The central idea

Identify the issuing member, eligible deposit and recorded coverage category first. Buying through another channel does not automatically create another limit for a client-name deposit.

01

Follow the deposit to its issuing member

A brokerage statement can contain a GIC issued by another financial institution. A separate statement does not by itself establish a separate deposit-insurance limit. The issuer, recorded ownership and applicable category determine which balances need to be considered together.

CDIC’s GIC guidance distinguishes deposits placed by a broker in the client’s name from deposits held by a broker as nominee. It states that client-name eligible deposits are combined with other deposits in the same insurance category at the same issuing member. This guide models only that client-name case.

Begin the inventory with the issuing institution shown in the deposit documentation, rather than stopping at the platform or advisor that arranged it. Verify membership and the product’s eligibility independently. A brand, branch or statement label is not sufficient evidence that two rows belong to different members.

Members A and B in the tool are invented and assumed genuinely distinct. They are not placeholders for a verified mapping of any named financial group. Nominee-name and trust arrangements require their own records and rules; this snapshot does not calculate their coverage.

02

Put the balances into a member-by-category map

The illustration uses one depositor and two qualifying categories at each member: eligible deposits in the one-name non-registered category and eligible deposits held in a TFSA. Direct and client-name brokered holdings are separate input channels inside each cell.

CDIC’s overview states a CAD 100,000 limit, including principal and interest, for each covered category at a member institution. Its TFSA examples also distinguish eligible deposits from securities held inside the same wrapper. The account wrapper alone does not make every product an eligible deposit.

All entered amounts are therefore assumed to be eligible deposits, already in place and correctly recorded in the stated categories. They include accrued interest through one common observation date. The calculator does not turn a security into a deposit, validate ownership or determine TFSA contribution room.

The first stacked chart makes the grouping visible. A directly held deposit and a client-name brokered GIC in the same cell are two parts of one combined eligible balance. The channels remain visible for reconciliation while the coverage cap is applied to their sum.

03

Reconcile the original four buckets

Member A’s one-name cell contains CAD 60,000 directly and CAD 50,000 through the client-name broker channel. Its total is CAD 110,000, of which CAD 100,000 is within the modeled cap and CAD 10,000 is above it.

A’s TFSA cell contains CAD 40,000 directly and CAD 70,000 through the client-name broker channel. It also totals CAD 110,000, with the same CAD 10,000 above its own separate modeled cap.

At member B, the one-name cell combines CAD 30,000 and CAD 60,000, for CAD 90,000. The TFSA cell combines CAD 10,000 and CAD 20,000, for CAD 30,000. Both are within their respective assumed limits.

The eligible total is CAD 340,000. Applying the cap cell by cell leaves CAD 320,000 within the modeled limits and CAD 20,000 above them. The second stacked chart shows those pieces without treating a second purchase channel as another category.

04

Headroom belongs to the cell in which it exists

The headroom matrix subtracts each combined balance from CAD 100,000. Member A’s cells each show negative CAD 10,000. Member B shows positive CAD 10,000 in one-name deposits and positive CAD 70,000 in TFSA eligible deposits.

Adding those signed figures would produce positive CAD 60,000, but that does not erase the CAD 20,000 above A’s two limits. A positive amount in one member/category cannot simply be applied to another cell’s excess.

The same point appears in the total-cap shortcut. Four assumed caps add to CAD 400,000, which exceeds the CAD 340,000 eligible balance. Yet the actual cell-by-cell illustration still has CAD 20,000 above individual limits. A combined maximum is not automatically usable when deposits are concentrated unevenly.

The waterfall checks the correct sequence: begin with CAD 340,000, subtract each of the two CAD 10,000 excesses and retain CAD 320,000. Coverage is aggregated after each separate bucket is tested. The matrix describes an existing snapshot, rather than approving a move between institutions or account wrappers.

05

Changing the channel alone does not change the combined balance

Within the same client-name member/category, relabeling CAD 20,000 from directly held to brokered holdings leaves the combined balance and this model’s coverage result unchanged. Only the first chart’s channel composition changes.

That invariance is useful for checking an inventory spread across several statements. Sum the compatible deposits before applying a cap. Do not count the same underlying deposit twice because it appears in a platform summary as well as an issuer record, and do not omit other eligible balances at that issuer.

Use the legal issuer and ownership records to establish the grouping. CDIC’s public member list is the reference for current members and associated trade names; this article does not verify any actual names. If the documentation instead shows nominee ownership or a trust relationship, stop applying this client-name illustration to it and consult the relevant rules.

Other registered categories, joint deposits, trust beneficiaries and provincial credit-union arrangements have separate requirements. They are outside this four-cell model. Their presence in a real household inventory calls for additional correctly classified rows, not an invented extra cap on an existing cell.

06

Keep protection, balance growth and access on separate schedules

The calculation is a same-date snapshot. It projects no interest, new deposit, withdrawal or tax payment. Future credited interest can change the balance relative to a cap, which is why the related headroom guide follows growth over time.

An above-cap amount is not a predicted loss, and an amount within the assumed limits is not proof that it can be spent today. A non-redeemable GIC still has contractual access and maturity conditions. Deposit protection addresses eligible deposits in a member failure; it does not replace the household payment calendar.

The useful review record identifies the observation date, issuer, ownership category, eligible product, principal and accrued interest. Keep the original documents that support those classifications, and check current CDIC guidance when circumstances or rules change.

These four charts organize that review. They preserve the purchase channels for reconciliation, apply limits to the correct combined cells, and prevent unused headroom elsewhere from hiding an excess. The result is an inspectable planning illustration rather than a coverage certificate or a deposit-transfer recommendation.

Sources and scope

Public sources reviewed on 25 October 2026. Balances and institutions are hypothetical. The snapshot applies selected current CDIC public guidance reviewed 25 October 2026 under explicit eligibility and client-name assumptions. It verifies no actual account, issuer, ownership record or contribution permission. Original scenario calculations and research checklists are TickerLantern’s educational analysis; attributed publisher examples retain their stated source and scope. Recheck current issuer documents for any product-specific decision.

  1. CDIC · Guaranteed Investment Certificates ↗

  2. CDIC · What is covered ↗

    Reviewed 25 October 2026. Supplies the CAD 100,000 principal-plus-interest limit per qualifying category at each member and the eligible-product distinction. All balances and member identities in the charts are invented.

  3. CDIC · Deposits held in a TFSA ↗

    Reviewed 25 October 2026 for eligible deposits versus securities inside a TFSA. The model determines neither tax eligibility nor contribution room.

  4. CDIC · Deposits held in one name ↗

    Reviewed 25 October 2026 for combining compatible savings, chequing and term deposits in this category. The input inventory must include all such eligible balances for the assumed depositor/member.

  5. CDIC · Member institutions and trade names ↗

    Reviewed 25 October 2026 as the official verification destination. No actual member/brand relationship is asserted in the hypothetical A/B example.
